page: Amazon Web Services r8id.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. It includes 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2156.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 34.41 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 4321.26 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 28.7 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth is also on the lower end, measuring 39.12 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though write bandwidth remains average at 29.24 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the r8id.xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside fast local NVMe storage, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high memory capacity without massive parallel processing needs. The primary tradeoff lies in its limited multi-core scaling and lower read-only memory bandwidth. This hardware profile is best suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, Redis caching, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
